scope: Theorem 8.2 (Scalar mesh projection) of the manuscript “Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension” (preprints/Every-four-dimensional-Kakeya-set-has-full-Hausdorff-dimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 30d0c186aa9c697d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 118. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ν be a probability law on trajectories (t, y(t), x(t)), where y is scalar affine, x is scalar quadratic, and all coefficients are bounded by K = No(1). Additional trajectory coordinates are permitted. Let µact ≤ Kν ⊗ dt have mass at least 1/K. Fix a = N−s, s > 0, and a dyadic mesh σ ∼log,N N−M in (t, y), with fixed M > s. Suppose c > 0 and its reciprocal are polynomially bounded and, for some d < 1, • each (t, y)-mesh cell and x-bin of width p = N−r, 0 ≤ r ≤ s, have active mass at most Kσ2cpd; • the number of occupied (σ, σ, a)-cells, multiplied by σ2, is at most Kc−1a−d. The depth hypotheses use fixed powers, with the rounding and interpolation conventions of Section 2. They imply d ≥ 0: otherwise summing the unit-width cap over terminal support contradicts the dense total mass. After a dense restriction and passage to a subsequence, there are labels with disjoint trajectory assignments and a common scale σ/K ≤ β ≤ K, up to subpower factors, such that each label has • a moving affine interval of width Kβ containing its assigned y-trajectories throughout unit time; • a quadratic F(t, y) with |x − F(t, y)| ≤ Ka throughout unit time on its assigned trajectories; • assigned active mass at least cadβ/K. The quadratic norm is at most K in coordinates adapted to the moving interval of scale β. If, at r = s, appending a y′-bin of width N−u gives the mass ceiling a further factor KN−S1u for 0 < u ≤ u1, with fixed S1, u1 > 0, then β ∼log,N 1.
